text_blocks.snippet: To boil eggs, lower cold eggs into boiling water, cook for 6 to 12 minutes depending on your preferred yolk, and cool them in ice water.
snippet_highlighted_words: lower cold eggs into boiling water, cook for 6 to 12 minutes depending on your preferred yolk, and cool them in ice water

list.snippet: Boil water: Fill a pot with enough water to fully cover the eggs and bring it to a rolling boil. Add a pinch of salt if you like.
Add the eggs: Take cold eggs straight from the fridge. Use a slotted spoon to gently lower them into the boiling water one by one.
Set a timer: Lower the heat slightly to keep a gentle boil and start your timer right away.
Cool the eggs: Prepare a bowl of cold water and ice cubes. When the timer goes off, use a spoon to move the eggs straight into the ice bath for 3 to 5 minutes.
6 minutes: Soft-boiled with a warm, runny yolk and soft whites.
8 minutes: Jammy yolk that is thick and gooey.
10 to 12 minutes: Hard-boiled with a firm yolk and whites, great for salads or lunchboxes.
Tap and roll: Gently tap the cooled egg on a hard surface to crack the shell all over.

Peel under water: Roll the egg gently in your hands, then peel the shell off starting from the wider bottom end. Doing this under cold running water or inside your ice bowl helps the shell slide off smoothly.
